intuition.summary: Closed-but-not-exact forms detect holes: a closed form with nonzero integral around a loop cannot have a global primitive, so the loop must encircle something missing from the space.
intuition.source: Petrov, The Essence of de Rham Cohomology (arXiv:2411.06296)

intuition.summary: Cohomology as 'all solutions modulo obvious solutions': in each degree, solutions of d=0 modulo those coming from a potential; the leftover counts global obstructions.
intuition.source: A. López Neumann, Du rotationnel à la cohomologie de de Rham (slides, Paris-Saclay "Explique-moi", 2021)

intuition.summary: De Rham cohomology measures how badly the fundamental theorem of calculus (zero derivative implies constant; closed implies has a potential) fails globally; slides attribute this phrasing to Tao.
intuition.source: A. López Neumann, Du rotationnel à la cohomologie de de Rham (slides, Paris-Saclay "Explique-moi", 2021)

intuition.summary: Vector-calculus picture: closed 1-form = curl-free field, exact 1-form = gradient; H^1 asks whether every curl-free field has a potential.
intuition.source: D. Perkinson (Reed College Math 341), lecture slides 08fri

intuition.summary: Closed forms are always locally exact (local branches of the angle differ by constants), so cohomology is a purely global, topological phenomenon.
intuition.source: Wikipedia, Closed and exact differential forms

intuition.summary: Dual picture via homology: cycles that do not bound are 'real holes'; de Rham classes are detected by integrating over them, and de Rham's theorem makes cohomology dual to homology.
intuition.source: A. López Neumann, Du rotationnel à la cohomologie de de Rham (slides, Paris-Saclay "Explique-moi", 2021)

intuition.summary: Harmonic representative picture: on a compact Riemannian manifold each class has a unique energy-minimizing (harmonic) representative, making classes concrete objects.

motivation.summary: Bott-Tu present de Rham theory as a computable model cohomology theory, with Mayer-Vietoris as the key tool, used to reach harder topology (characteristic classes, spectral sequences, homotopy).
motivation.source: Bott & Tu, Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, Intro and §1-§5

motivation.summary: Path independence / conservative fields: integrals of exact forms around closed loops vanish (Stokes); de Rham cohomology classifies when potentials exist.
motivation.source: Petrov, The Essence of de Rham Cohomology (arXiv:2411.06296)

motivation.summary: Historical: de Rham (1931) proved integration over chains identifies these groups with real singular cohomology; Weil (1952) gave a Čech-based proof.
motivation.source: Wikipedia, De Rham cohomology and Wikipedia, De Rham theorem

motivation.summary: Physics origin: magnetic field as a closed 2-form (no monopoles) with vector potential; Coulomb field on R^3 minus a point represents a nonzero H^2 class (charge).
motivation.source: Wikipedia, Closed and exact differential forms; Bott & Tu, Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, Intro and §1-§5

motivation.summary: Topological invariants from calculus: H^*(S^n) computes to R in degrees 0,n, giving invariance of dimension for R^n.
motivation.source: A. López Neumann, Du rotationnel à la cohomologie de de Rham (slides, Paris-Saclay "Explique-moi", 2021)

motivation.summary: Arithmetic motivation: Grothendieck's algebraic de Rham cohomology gives a K-structure on complex cohomology; comparing with Betti rational structure produces periods.
motivation.source: K. Kedlaya, Notes on prismatic cohomology, Overview section

definitions.summary: Standard: H^k_dR(M) = ker(d: Ω^k→Ω^{k+1}) / im(d: Ω^{k-1}→Ω^k); well-defined because d^2=0. Graded-commutative ring under wedge.
On R^n Bott-Tu define Ω*(R^n) = C^∞ ⊗ Λ(dx_1..dx_n) with anticommuting dx_i, then glue; also define compactly supported Ω*_c and H*_c.
definitions.source: Bott & Tu, Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, Intro and §1-§5

definitions.summary: Sheaf definition: the de Rham complex is a fine resolution of the constant sheaf R (Poincaré lemma = exactness), so H_dR = sheaf cohomology H(M;R); agreement proved by acyclicity of fine sheaves.
Algebraic: for smooth varieties, algebraic de Rham cohomology is hypercohomology of the algebraic de Rham complex Ω^•_X; singular varieties need Grothendieck's more subtle version.

De Rham theorem via integration map I: [ω]↦(c↦∫_c ω) on smooth singular chains, well defined by Stokes; proved iso by Mayer-Vietoris + five lemma induction over good covers/bases ('de Rham manifolds').
definitions.source: D. Chua, Part III Differential Geometry notes, ch.7 De Rham's theorem; Ginory, De Rham's Theorem (Rutgers notes); Petrov, The Essence of de Rham Cohomology (arXiv:2411.06296)

definitions.summary: Smooth singular homology equals ordinary singular homology (smoothing of simplices compatible with faces), needed so integration makes sense.

Alternative proof via sheaves/hypercohomology; and a version with currents that loses multiplicativity. Integration pairing with homology is perfect: a closed form is exact iff all its periods vanish.
Abstract: Ω•(M) as Chevalley-Eilenberg algebra of the tangent Lie algebroid; cohesive-homotopy version ♭_dR A.

viewpoints.summary: Analytic/Hodge: harmonic forms (kernel of Δ=dδ+δd) represent classes uniquely on closed manifolds; with boundary use tangential/normal conditions for absolute/relative cohomology.
Discrete/numerical: cochains on a mesh with coboundary, Whitney map and de Rham map commuting with d, mimicking the smooth complex; Poincaré operators become cone operators.
Physics: conserved currents are closed forms, charges are periods over cycles, topological invariance of charge operators is Stokes; gauge freedom = adding exact forms.
Equivariant: Cartan model complex (S(g*)⊗Ω)^G with d_G = d - Σ ξ^i ι_i computes Borel equivariant cohomology; localization of integrals.
Arithmetic: comparison H_dR⊗C≅H_B⊗C; in char p and over Z_p de Rham behaves differently (Cartier isomorphism, crystalline, prismatic); Poincaré lemma fails in char p.
viewpoints.source: K. Kedlaya, Notes on prismatic cohomology, Overview section; Prismatic cohomology course, Lecture I Overview (Bhatt, Columbia; author not printed on page)

viewpoints.summary: Characteristic classes: invariant polynomials of curvature give closed forms whose de Rham classes are independent of the connection (Chern-Weil).

conventions.summary: Graded commutativity ω∧φ=(-1)^{pq}φ∧ω and antiderivation d(ω∧φ)=dω∧φ+(-1)^p ω∧dφ; Bott-Tu fix the boundary orientation of the half space with a (-1)^n so Stokes has no sign; homotopy operator identity carries a sign (-1)^{k-1}.
conventions.source: Bott & Tu, Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, Intro and §1-§5

conventions.summary: Two normalisations of wedge/alternation: most modern texts vs Kobayashi-Nomizu and Helgason; the coordinate-free formula for d then differs by a constant factor (believed 1/(k+1)).
Codifferential sign δ=(-1)^{m(k-1)+1} * d * in one paper; other sources use (-1)^{m(k+1)+1} or (-1)^k *^{-1}d*; check the source.
Cartan differential sign: d_G = d - Σ ξ^i ι_{ξ_i} (Notman-Sanabani); other authors use d + ι or include factors of i or 2π; Euler class/localization signs depend on this.
Chern class normalisation: either c(E)=det(1+ (i/2π)F) or with -1/(2πi); characteristic polynomial in t vs t^{-1}; Wikipedia notes its sign choice.
Notation: H^k_dR(M), H^k(M;R), H_dR^k(X/K) (algebraic), H_c^k compact support; Lee and Petrov use smooth singular chains; Ginory indexes chain complexes by all integers.
conventions.source: Ginory, De Rham's Theorem (Rutgers notes); Petrov, The Essence of de Rham Cohomology (arXiv:2411.06296); arXiv:2206.08618

conventions.summary: Tate twist convention Q(k)=(2πi)^k Q to make the comparison isomorphism and cycle classes compatible.

examples.summary: Circle: H^0=H^1=R; dθ is closed, not exact, integral 2π; ring R[x]/(x^2). Generator built via Mayer-Vietoris and bump function in Bott-Tu.
examples.source: Gualtieri, MAT1300 notes §6.2-6.6; Bott & Tu, Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, Intro and §1-§5

examples.summary: Punctured plane R^2\{0}: angle form closed not exact; same cohomology as circle.
examples.source: Wikipedia, Closed and exact differential forms; Petrov, The Essence of de Rham Cohomology (arXiv:2411.06296)

examples.summary: Spheres S^n: R in degrees 0 and n via Mayer-Vietoris with two charts.
examples.source: Gualtieri, MAT1300 notes §6.2-6.6; nLab, de Rham cohomology

examples.summary: Tori T^n: dim H^k = C(n,k), generated by wedges of dθ_i (Künneth).
R^3 minus a line has curl-free non-gradient fields; R^3 minus a point is simply connected but has div-free fields that are not curls (H^1=0, H^2≠0).
examples.source: A. López Neumann, Du rotationnel à la cohomologie de de Rham (slides, Paris-Saclay "Explique-moi", 2021)

examples.summary: Möbius strip has the cohomology of the circle (homotopy invariance); compact supported H_c^*(R^n)=R in degree n only.
examples.source: Wikipedia, De Rham cohomology; Bott & Tu, Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, Intro and §1-§5

examples.summary: Torsion counterexamples: Klein bottle / RP^n integral torsion invisible to de Rham; Enriques surface 2-torsion in H^2; in char 2 Enriques surfaces have nonzero H^1_dR.
examples.source: Wikipedia, De Rham theorem; K. Kedlaya, Notes on prismatic cohomology, Overview section; Prismatic cohomology course, Lecture I Overview (Bhatt, Columbia; author not printed on page)

examples.summary: Closed oriented n-manifold: H^n≠0 since a volume form has nonzero integral and exact top forms integrate to 0.
examples.source: D. Perkinson (Reed College Math 341), lecture slides 08fri

computation.summary: Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence (from partition-of-unity short exact sequence) plus induction on good covers.
computation.source: Bott & Tu, Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, Intro and §1-§5; Gualtieri, MAT1300 notes §6.2-6.6

computation.summary: Homotopy invariance via chain homotopy integrating along [0,1]; reduce to deformation retracts.
Poincaré duality pairing H^k × H_c^{n-k}→R and Künneth formula for products.
computation.source: Guillemin & Haine, Differential Forms, Ch.3 and Ch.5; Petrov, The Essence of de Rham Cohomology (arXiv:2411.06296)

computation.summary: Good covers / Čech-de Rham double complex: cohomology equals Čech cohomology of the nerve with R coefficients.
computation.source: Bott & Tu, Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, Intro and §1-§5; Guillemin & Haine, Differential Forms, Ch.3 and Ch.5

computation.summary: Hodge theory: compute dim of harmonic forms; discrete versions compute kernels of Hodge Laplacian matrices on meshes.
Periods test: closed form is exact iff all integrals over cycles vanish; use integrals to show non-exactness.
Compact connected Lie groups: cohomology computed by bi-invariant forms / Lie algebra cohomology.
Chern-Weil: compute characteristic classes from any convenient connection's curvature.

confusions.summary: 'Closed implies exact' only locally; globally fails; the angle 'function' is multivalued but its differential is a well-defined form.
confusions.source: Wikipedia, Closed and exact differential forms

confusions.summary: Simply connected suffices for H^1=0 but not for higher degrees (R^3 minus a point has H^2≠0). Wikipedia's summary loosely conflates contractible and simply connected.
confusions.source: A. López Neumann, Du rotationnel à la cohomologie de de Rham (slides, Paris-Saclay "Explique-moi", 2021); Wikipedia, De Rham cohomology

confusions.summary: De Rham uses real coefficients: torsion in integral cohomology is lost; integral of a form over a torsion class is zero.
confusions.source: Wikipedia, De Rham theorem; Prismatic cohomology course, Lecture I Overview (Bhatt, Columbia; author not printed on page)

confusions.summary: Singular simplices are merely continuous; one must pass to smooth singular chains before integrating, then show nothing is lost.
confusions.source: Petrov, The Essence of de Rham Cohomology (arXiv:2411.06296); Ginory, De Rham's Theorem (Rutgers notes)

confusions.summary: Compactly supported cohomology is covariant for open inclusions, not functorial under all smooth maps; Poincaré duality pairs H^k with H_c^{n-k}, not H^k with H^{n-k}, on noncompact manifolds.
confusions.source: Bott & Tu, Differential Forms in Algebraic Topology, Intro and §1-§5; Petrov, The Essence of de Rham Cohomology (arXiv:2411.06296)

confusions.summary: With boundary, harmonic fields (closed and coclosed) are infinite-dimensional; need boundary conditions to get finite-dimensional spaces matching absolute or relative cohomology.
Normalisation of wedge/alternation changes formulas for d by constants across books; check conventions.
